title: Righteous Deeds and Divine Response
english: The usefulness of righteous deeds is not moderate for those who see them. Indeed, Christ said to his holy apostles: ‘Let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.’ Therefore, we shall be radiant, carried about and as it were clothed with the glory from God, to those to whom he might grant justice as caretakers.

Having existed for you, he says, you will cry out then, and God will hear you. Even while you are still speaking, he will say: ‘Behold, I have come.’ For the prayer of the righteous he hears, as it is written. And as the Melodist says: ‘The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are open to their petition.’ He nods indeed to those who ask, as a good God, but not to all immediately.

To those, however, who have been conspicuous in righteousness, without any longing, he stretches out their petitions and holds most ready their hearing, so that, in regard to each of their requests, they rejoice and say: ‘He heard my voice from his holy temple, and my cry entered into his ears.’ Thus, the surpassing earnestness of ambition, and the very readiness of the giving God, are plainly set forth in the cry, ‘Behold, I have come,’ still speaking of the righteous, stretching out their petitions.

If you remove from yourself bond, hand-raising, and murmuring speech, and give your bread to the hungry, and satisfy the humbled soul, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkness will be at noon, and your God will be with you always. The exceptional lessons, even if often said to some, nevertheless have their usefulness.

The all-wise Paul writes to those who came to faith through him, saying that repeating the same teachings is no burden to him but is for their safety. Thus, through these same teachings, he speaks to us in many ways, making clear the paths to success and recounting the joy of the gifts promised to the saints, so that he might stir us to greater zeal in doing the deeds by which we may become venerable, and we shall discover the ambition that comes from above and from him.

Therefore, he says, 'If you remove from yourselves a bond and an ordination.' And by bond he means, as I understand, the depravity of the nations, their shamelessness, their love of strife, and the practice of forming alliances against others for selfish ends, as well as inventing crooked schemes to entrap people, sometimes binding them with fetters and bringing upon them helpless circumstances.

For a person must be simple and approachable if they are to look toward God and cling to the graces that come from him. But by ordination he perhaps means, in some places, the love of bribes and the pursuit of shameful gain, which we do indeed sometimes observe.

title: Faith and Righteousness
english: The demonstration of faith becomes the means by which unbelievers are saved from their hopes, and the hand of the savior is extended to those who are on the ground, just as we live in this world. But what do those who bring forth the set stone have to say about this? For from the foundation of the world, we have neither heard nor seen a God like you, except for you alone, to whom those who have been persuaded have placed their hope, and you have increased mercy to those who do the works of righteousness.

The prophet David says, 'In your way, I will be saved,' and again, 'I will walk in your ways, when I have set my heart right.' Behold, you have worked, and we have sinned; the Lord says that his commands are to be kept, and he fulfills the desires of the saints.

We were deceived and became completely unclean, and our righteousness was taken away from us. We were scattered like leaves because of our iniquities, and the name that is called upon us is not yours. The memory of you is that you turned your face away from us and delivered us because of our sins. God gave some things to our enemies, and according to another thought, he threw the preceding things at them.

The reward of our words is the power of our thoughts, and this is why such things happen as it is said: 'Behold, we sin, and you are angry.' However, God is not the cause of sin, but the wrath of God was stirred up because of our actions. Since we have sinned, God is angry, for it is not according to his image that he thinks to conceive sin. It seems necessary to say that the wrath of God does not have the power to destroy, but rather the power to destroy the sins that were done against him is able to flee.

As long as the Savior is with us, we are glad and boast of our sins, despising the reproaches of the foolish and being crowned with the spiritual crown. But when we are tested by the power of righteousness and the first of virtue, we fall into weakness and are unable to stand.
